mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary policy regime that increases discount rates for equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the average forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals tightening labor market conditions that increase wage pressures and inflation expectations, prompting central bank hawkishness and reducing equity risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in over 60% of cases when UNRATE < 4.0%, or the mean forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential construction permits above 1.3 million units signals strong household demand and confidence, which drives inflationary expectations and raises the likelihood of monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered instances, or the average forward return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production and a rise in the unemployment rate signals a weakening manufacturing sector and labor market stress, indicating an imminent economic slowdown that reduces corporate earnings growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases where both INDPRO < 102.0 and UNRATE > 4.1%, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) above 715 billion dollars signals strong consumer demand, which supports corporate revenues and earnings growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances despite RSAFS > 715B, or the average forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPIAUCSL above 315.0 with a 12-month growth rate exceeding 3.5% signals persistent inflation, increasing the probability of further rate hikes, which depresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 315.0 and 12mo_growth > 3.5%, or the average return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in payroll employment and a decline in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market that boosts consumer spending and inflationary pressures, increasing the likelihood of monetary tightening and reducing equity risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases where PAYEMS > 159000.0 and UNRATE < 4.3%, or the joint signal fails to produce a statistically significant negative return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in real GDP (GDPC1) above 23300 billion dollars signals strong economic momentum, which supports corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX generates negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances despite GDPC1 > 23300B, or the average forward return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).
